findings.F1: The book fails on its size, not its sign: its mean daily return is 0.000496 against 0.0005 and its Calmar 0.71 against 0.75; per case the unusual move is +0.20 % over 3 days against a round trip of 0.19 % (1.1 times), so the edge the book bets on barely covers its cost.
findings.F2: The edge sits in how decisively the bar breaks out, not in how quiet the week was: with the close's distance above the prior 2-day high measured in units of the 7-day mean 4h range, the top fifth of breakouts has an unusual move of +1.31 % over 3 days (t 3.39, 590 cases), while the four lower fifths range from -0.77 % to +0.59 % (t -2.39 to 1.31).
findings.F3: The breakout bar's own return in units of the 7-day mean range grades the same way: the top fifth has +1.21 % (t 3.08, 590 cases) and the bottom fifth -0.54 % (t -1.79).
findings.F4: The quietness ratio the book sizes by grades weakly and not in order: by fifths the unusual move is +0.45 %, -0.08 %, -0.33 %, +0.55 % and +0.78 % (t of the top fifth 1.73, 311 cases).
findings.F5: The book's position follows the weak variable: it correlates 0.40 with the quietness ratio and only 0.12 with breakout strength, so its largest bets are not placed on the breakouts that carry the move.
findings.F6: Strong breakouts after a quiet week are the best cell: with both measures split into thirds, the strongest-and-quietest cell has an unusual move of +1.99 % (t 2.88, 184 cases), and the strongest-and-busiest cell +1.65 % (t 1.57, 158). The middle-strength thirds are all negative, from -0.49 % to -0.93 %.
findings.F7: The deepest fall of the book is 24 % over 597 days, from w5 to w10, while holding the coins lost 57.5 %. In those windows even the strongest fifth of breakouts earned only +0.27 % (t 0.49, 181 cases) against +1.77 % (t 3.55, 409 cases) elsewhere, and the book held more then (mean position 0.52 to 0.66 against 0.47 to 0.56).
findings.F8: The coin's 7-day return before the breakout grades the move: breakouts in the lowest fifth of 7-day return (mean -8.5 %) have an unusual move of -0.77 % (t -2.49, 589 cases), and those in the highest fifth (mean +24 %) have +1.04 % (t 1.96).

ideas.idea: When a four-hour bar closes above the highest high of a coin's preceding two-day stretch, the coin rises over the next three days. The rise is larger the further that close lies above the two-day high, measured against the coin's average four-hour range over the past 7 days, and larger still the quieter that 7-day range was compared with its 60-day average.
ideas.consequence: A trader should size an upward four-hour breakout mainly by how far the close clears the two-day high, in units of the past week's typical range, and only secondarily by the quietness of the week.
ideas.name: decisive breakout graded continuation

ideas.idea: When a four-hour bar closes above the highest high of a coin's preceding two-day stretch, the coin rises over the next three days. The rise is larger the quieter the coin's average four-hour range over the past 7 days was compared with its average over the past 60 days, and larger the higher the coin's 7-day return at the breakout.
ideas.consequence: A trader should give less weight to upward breakouts that come after a falling week, since these are the ones that fail inside long declines.
ideas.name: breakout after rising week

ideas.idea: The further a coin's four-hour close lies above the highest high of its preceding two days, measured against its average four-hour range over the past 7 days, the more the coin rises over the next three days.
ideas.consequence: A trader should treat the size of the push through a recent high, scaled by recent range, as a long signal in its own right.
ideas.name: breakout distance predicts rise
